    Frame property modifiers¶

    Passed as modifiers= on elasticBeamColumn, ElasticTimoshenkoBeam, forceBeamColumn and dispBeamColumn. The emitted section properties are the declared ones times the modifiers, in the way ETABS frame property modifiers work.

    apeGmsh.opensees.FrameModifiers dataclass ¶

    FrameModifiers(*, A: float = 1.0, Avy: float = 1.0, Avz: float = 1.0, J: float = 1.0, Iy: float = 1.0, Iz: float = 1.0, mass: float = 1.0, weight: float = 1.0)

    Frame section property modifiers, in OpenSees local axes.

    Every field defaults to 1.0 (gross section). The six stiffness modifiers (A, Avy, Avz, J, Iy, Iz) must be finite and > 0; mass and weight finite and >= 0.

    Attach to an element spec with modifiers=::

    cracked = FrameModifiers.etabs(I22=0.7, I33=0.7)   # ACI 318-25 columns
ops.element.elasticBeamColumn(pg="Cols", transf=t, A=..., E=...,
                              Iz=..., Iy=..., G=..., J=...,
                              modifiers=cracked)

    Use :meth:etabs to construct from ETABS-named modifiers.

    is_identity property ¶

    is_identity: bool

    True when every modifier is 1.0 (gross section).

    etabs classmethod ¶

    etabs(*, A: float = 1.0, As2: float = 1.0, As3: float = 1.0, J: float = 1.0, I22: float = 1.0, I33: float = 1.0, mass: float = 1.0, weight: float = 1.0) -> 'FrameModifiers'

    Build from ETABS frame property modifier names.

    Axis mapping: ETABS local 1 runs along the member, as OpenSees local x does. Choose the element's geomTransf vecxz along ETABS local 3: OpenSees local z then equals ETABS 3, and since both triads are right-handed with a common first axis, OpenSees local y = z x x = 3 x 1 = ETABS 2. Under that vecxz the mapping is As2 -> Avy, As3 -> Avz, I22 -> Iy (bending about local 2 / y), I33 -> Iz (bending about local 3 / z, the major axis of an ETABS frame section). A, J, mass and weight carry no axis. With any other vecxz the 2 and 3 modifiers land on whichever OpenSees axes it defines, so check it.

    For a vertical ETABS column (1 = +Z, 2 = +X, 3 = +Y) that is vecxz=(0, 1, 0); for a beam along +X (1 = +X, 2 = +Z, 3 = -Y) it is vecxz=(0, -1, 0).

    The ETABS importer does not use this convention. interop/etabs_import.py (_VECXZ) gives a vertical member vecxz=(1, 0, 0) and any other member (0, 0, 1): for a member at its default orientation both are ETABS 2, not 3, and the importer ignores Frame.rotation. Under that vecxz OpenSees local z is ETABS 2, so I33 lands on the minor axis (and I22 on the major one). The importer passes no modifiers= today; wiring it to this method needs vecxz along ETABS 3 first.

    @classmethod
def etabs(
    cls,
    *,
    A: float = 1.0,
    As2: float = 1.0,
    As3: float = 1.0,
    J: float = 1.0,
    I22: float = 1.0,
    I33: float = 1.0,
    mass: float = 1.0,
    weight: float = 1.0,
) -> "FrameModifiers":
    """Build from ETABS frame property modifier names.

    Axis mapping: ETABS local 1 runs along the member, as OpenSees
    local x does. Choose the element's ``geomTransf`` ``vecxz`` along
    **ETABS local 3**: OpenSees local z then equals ETABS 3, and since
    both triads are right-handed with a common first axis, OpenSees
    local y = z x x = 3 x 1 = ETABS 2. Under that ``vecxz`` the mapping
    is ``As2 -> Avy``, ``As3 -> Avz``, ``I22 -> Iy`` (bending about
    local 2 / y), ``I33 -> Iz`` (bending about local 3 / z, the major
    axis of an ETABS frame section). ``A``, ``J``, ``mass`` and
    ``weight`` carry no axis. With any other ``vecxz`` the 2 and 3
    modifiers land on whichever OpenSees axes it defines, so check it.

    For a vertical ETABS column (1 = +Z, 2 = +X, 3 = +Y) that is
    ``vecxz=(0, 1, 0)``; for a beam along +X (1 = +X, 2 = +Z,
    3 = -Y) it is ``vecxz=(0, -1, 0)``.

    **The ETABS importer does not use this convention.**
    ``interop/etabs_import.py`` (``_VECXZ``) gives a vertical member
    ``vecxz=(1, 0, 0)`` and any other member ``(0, 0, 1)``: for a member
    at its default orientation both are ETABS **2**, not 3, and the
    importer ignores ``Frame.rotation``. Under that ``vecxz`` OpenSees
    local z is ETABS 2, so ``I33`` lands on the minor axis (and ``I22``
    on the major one). The importer passes no ``modifiers=`` today;
    wiring it to this method needs ``vecxz`` along ETABS 3 first.
    """
    return cls(
        A=A, Avy=As2, Avz=As3, J=J, Iy=I22, Iz=I33,
        mass=mass, weight=weight,
    )

    Recorders¶

    Standalone recorder declaration helper. Recorder declarations live on ops.recorder.* in the apeSees bridge (typed primitives — Node / Element / MPCO / declarative fan-out via ops.recorder.declare(...)).

    apeGmsh.opensees.recorder ¶

    Typed recorder primitives.

    Phase 3B ships three concrete recorder classes mirroring the OpenSees recorder command:

    • :class:Node — recorder Node ...
    • :class:Element — recorder Element ...
    • :class:MPCO — recorder mpco ... (HDF5)

    Each class is a @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True, slots=True); the matching :class:apeGmsh.opensees._internal.ns.recorder._RecorderNS methods take the same kwargs and call self._bridge._register(Cls(...)).

    Recorders never compose other primitives (dependencies() returns ()). They are leaves in the dependency graph; the build pipeline emits them after the topology + analysis chain so that each recorder command sees fully-allocated node and element tags.

    The pg= form (physical-group fan-out into node/element tags) is materialized at build time by :func:apeGmsh.opensees._internal.build.recorders.emit_recorder_spec, which resolves pg through the FEM snapshot, rewrites the spec to its explicit nodes= / elements= form via :func:dataclasses.replace, and then delegates to _emit. End users drive this through apeSees(fem).tcl(...) / .py(...) / .run() — never call _emit directly with a pg spec, which raises :class:NotImplementedError as a defense-in-depth guard.

    OpenSees command shapes¶

    ::

    recorder Node    -file fname [-time] [-dT dT] [-node n...]
                             -dof d... response
recorder Element -file fname [-time] [-dT dT] [-ele e...]
                             response_tokens...
recorder mpco    fname.mpco  [-N nodal_responses...]
                             [-E elem_responses...]
                             [-T dt $dt | -T nsteps $n]

    The -time flag (when time_format="dt") instructs OpenSees to include the simulation-time column in the output file. The default time_format="step" writes only the response columns.

    Node dataclass ¶

    Node(*, file: str, response: str, nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, pg: str | None = None, label: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, dofs: tuple[int, ...], dT: float | None = None, time_format: str = 'step', precision: int | None = None)

    Bases: Recorder

    recorder Node — record nodal response history.

    OpenSees command::

    recorder Node -file fname [-time] [-dT dT]
              (-node n1 n2 ... | -nodeRange first last)
              -dof d1 d2 ... response

    Exactly one of nodes= (explicit list) or pg= (physical-group label) must be supplied. The bridge build pipeline materializes the pg= form against the FEM snapshot before driving _emit; direct _emit calls on a pg= spec raise :class:NotImplementedError as a defense-in-depth guard.

    Parameters¶

    file Output file path. response OpenSees response token ("disp", "vel", "accel", "reaction", "unbalance", ...). nodes Explicit tuple of node tags. Mutually exclusive with pg. pg Physical-group label whose nodes the recorder targets. Mutually exclusive with nodes. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time. label Provenance of an ops.recorder.Node(label=...) declaration (ADR 0115 amendment R2-f): the geometry label name(s) the call resolved to nodes. Never re-resolved and never emitted; nodes stays authoritative. Needs nodes=, refuses pg=. dofs DOF indices (1-based, OpenSees convention). At least one required. dT Optional cadence — record only every dT simulation seconds. None records every step. time_format "step" (default) writes only response columns; "dt" emits the OpenSees -time flag, prepending the simulation-time column. precision Significant digits per written value (OpenSees -precision N; its default is 6). None (default) emits no flag, so the deck is unchanged. A positive int; anything else raises.

    Element(*, file: str, response: tuple[str, ...], elements: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, pg: str | None = None, label: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, dT: float | None = None, time_format: str = 'step', precision: int | None = None)

    recorder Element — record element-level response history.

    OpenSees command::

    recorder Element -file fname [-time] [-dT dT]
                 (-ele e1 e2 ... | -eleRange first last)
                 response_tokens...

    response is a tuple of OpenSees response tokens — the simplest case is ("globalForce",) or ("stresses",); element types that nest responses (e.g. fiber sections) take multi-token forms such as ("section", "1", "force").

    Exactly one of elements= (explicit list) or pg= (physical- group label) must be supplied. pg= is resolved against the FEM snapshot by the bridge build pipeline before driving _emit; direct _emit calls on a pg= spec raise :class:NotImplementedError as a defense-in-depth guard.

    Parameters¶

    file Output file path. response Tuple of OpenSees response tokens (at least one). elements Explicit tuple of element tags. Mutually exclusive with pg. With label set they are the FEM element ids the label resolved to, which the bridge translates to the emitted OpenSees tags at build (as it does for pg=). pg Physical-group label whose elements the recorder targets. Mutually exclusive with elements. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time. label Provenance of an ops.recorder.Element(label=...) declaration (ADR 0115 amendment R2-f): the geometry label name(s) the call resolved to FEM element ids. Never re-resolved and never emitted; it marks elements as FEM ids. Needs elements=, refuses pg=. The archive stores the translated OpenSees tags, as for every other Element recorder. dT Optional cadence — record only every dT simulation seconds. None records every step. time_format "step" (default) writes only response columns; "dt" emits the OpenSees -time flag. precision Significant digits per written value (OpenSees -precision N; its default is 6). None (default) emits no flag, so the deck is unchanged. A positive int; anything else raises.

    FilterableRecorder dataclass ¶

    FilterableRecorder(*, file: str, nodal_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), elem_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), dT: float | None = None, nsteps: int | None = None, nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, nodes_pg: str | None = None, elements: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, elements_pg: str | None = None, _region_tag: int | None = None)

    Bases: Recorder

    Base for HDF5 recorders that share MPCO's region-filter surface.

    Carries the four mutually-paired selectors (nodes / nodes_pg / elements / elements_pg) and the region-emit machinery that turns them into an OpenSees region $tag -node ... -ele ... line plus a -R $tag on the recorder command. :class:MPCO and :class:Ladruno both inherit it; they differ only in the recorder kind token and (Ladruno) the trailing -G energy channel.

    Carries the shared value channels too (file + nodal_responses / elem_responses -N/-E + dT/nsteps -T cadence), so :meth:_value_channel_args builds the common -N ... -E ... -T ... -R ... tail once for both subclasses — only the recorder kind token and (Ladruno) the trailing -G energy are subclass-specific.

    Subclasses own only their required-response rule (MPCO needs nodal or element responses; Ladruno also accepts energy); the cadence mutex (:meth:_validate_cadence) and the four selector guards (:meth:_validate_filter) are shared. The partition-aware build pipeline (ADR 0027 INV-4) keys its per-rank region pass on isinstance(spec, FilterableRecorder) via :meth:has_filter / :meth:resolve_filter_ids.

    True iff any node/element selector was supplied.

    Used by the partition-aware build pipeline (ADR 0027 INV-4) to decide whether the recorder needs a per-rank region pass — a whole-model recorder (no filter) emits one recorder line and nothing else.

    def has_filter(self) -> bool:
    """True iff any node/element selector was supplied.

    Used by the partition-aware build pipeline (ADR 0027 INV-4) to
    decide whether the recorder needs a per-rank region pass — a
    whole-model recorder (no filter) emits one ``recorder`` line
    and nothing else.
    """
    return (
        self.nodes is not None
        or self.nodes_pg is not None
        or self.elements is not None
        or self.elements_pg is not None
    )

    region_keys ¶

    region_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]

    def region_keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The regions this recorder writes, in the order they take tags.

    ``"filter"`` is the value-channel filter region (``-R``), present
    iff :meth:`has_filter`. :class:`Ladruno` adds ``"energy"``, its
    decoupled energy region. The tag plan numbers them in this order.
    """
    return ("filter",) if self.has_filter() else ()

    def planned_region_tags(
    self, fem: "FEMData", tag_plan: "TagPlan",
) -> dict[object, int]:
    """The tag of each of :meth:`region_keys`, by key.

    Read from ``tag_plan`` (ADR 0114 D4, amended): a plan made for

    raises :class:`~._internal.build.errors.TagPlanMiss`.

    def resolve_filter_ids(
    self,
    fem: "FEMData",
    fem_eid_to_ops_tag: "FemToOpsTagMap | dict[int, int] | None" = None,
) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Resolve ``nodes`` / ``nodes_pg`` / ``elements`` / ``elements_pg``
    to explicit id tuples — no emission, no tag allocation.

    Returns ``(node_ids, elem_ids)``. Either may be empty when its
    side was not requested; an empty *result* on a *requested* side
    (e.g. ``nodes_pg="X"`` resolving to zero nodes) raises
    :class:`BridgeError` to mirror the OpenSees runtime rejection of
    an empty region.

    ``fem_eid_to_ops_tag`` is the bridge-built ``{fem_eid: ops_tag}``
    map for element fan-out.  When supplied AND ``elements_pg`` is
    set, the resolved FEM eids are translated to OpenSees element
    tags before they flow into the region's ``-ele`` arg list
    (same drift as the Element recorder, closed by
    :meth:`Element.materialize`).  Lookup miss → :class:`BridgeError`.
    When ``None`` (legacy direct callers) the FEM eids are returned
    verbatim — the partition orchestrator uses this form so it can
    intersect per-rank in FEM-eid space, then translate at the
    final region-emit step.

    This is the partition-aware split-point of the legacy single-
    pass :meth:`materialize`: the partition orchestrator calls
    ``resolve_filter_ids`` once globally to determine the full
    filter id set, then intersects per-rank before emitting the
    region.  Whole-model recording (``has_filter() is False``) is
    a no-op pass-through — callers should not invoke this method
    in that case.
    """
    from ._internal.build.errors import BridgeError
    from ._internal.build.pg_expand import (
        expand_pg_to_elements,
        expand_pg_to_nodes,
    )

    kind = type(self).__name__

    # Resolve node-side selector.
    node_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    if self.nodes_pg is not None:
        node_ids = expand_pg_to_nodes(fem, self.nodes_pg)
        if not node_ids:
            raise BridgeError(
                f"{kind} recorder filter: nodes_pg={self.nodes_pg!r} "
                "resolved to zero nodes against the FEM snapshot. "
                "An empty region is rejected by OpenSees at runtime; "
                "check the PG name spelling and that the PG was "
                "populated before get_fem_data."
            )
    elif self.nodes is not None:
        node_ids = tuple(int(n) for n in self.nodes)
        if not node_ids:
            raise BridgeError(
                f"{kind} recorder filter: nodes=() is empty.  An empty "
                "region is rejected by OpenSees at runtime; supply a "
                "non-empty tuple or drop the nodes= kwarg."
            )

    # Resolve element-side selector.
    elem_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    if self.elements_pg is not None:
        fem_eids = tuple(
            eid for eid, _conn in expand_pg_to_elements(fem, self.elements_pg)
        )
        if not fem_eids:
            raise BridgeError(
                f"{kind} recorder filter: elements_pg={self.elements_pg!r} "
                "resolved to zero elements against the FEM snapshot. "
                "An empty region is rejected by OpenSees at runtime; "
                "check the PG name spelling and that elements were "
                "registered against it before get_fem_data."
            )
        if fem_eid_to_ops_tag is None:
            # Legacy / partition-orchestrator form: return FEM eids
            # verbatim so the caller can intersect per-rank in
            # FEM-eid space.  The bridge's flat path always supplies
            # the map; the partition path translates at the final
            # per-rank region-emit step.
            elem_ids = fem_eids
        else:
            ops_tags: list[int] = []
            for eid in fem_eids:
                ops_tag = fem_eid_to_ops_tag.get(int(eid))
                if ops_tag is None:
                    raise BridgeError(
                        f"{kind} recorder filter: elements_pg="
                        f"{self.elements_pg!r} resolves to FEM eid "
                        f"{eid} but no element was emitted at that "
                        "eid — declare an "
                        "``ops.element.X(pg=...)`` primitive whose "
                        f"pg includes {self.elements_pg!r}."
                    )
                ops_tags.append(int(ops_tag))
            elem_ids = tuple(ops_tags)
    elif self.elements is not None:
        elem_ids = tuple(int(e) for e in self.elements)
        if not elem_ids:
            raise BridgeError(
                f"{kind} recorder filter: elements=() is empty.  An "
                "empty region is rejected by OpenSees at runtime; "
                "supply a non-empty tuple or drop the elements= kwarg."
            )

    return node_ids, elem_ids

    materialize ¶

    materialize(emitter: 'Emitter', fem: 'FEMData', tag_plan: 'TagPlan | None', fem_eid_to_ops_tag: 'FemToOpsTagMap | dict[int, int] | None' = None) -> 'FilterableRecorder'

    Resolve filter selectors against the FEM and emit the region.

    Whole-model recording (no filter selectors) is a no-op pass- through. When any of nodes / nodes_pg / elements / elements_pg is set, this method:

    1. Resolves *_pg to explicit id tuples via the bridge's PG-expansion helpers; refuses empty resolutions with :class:BridgeError (an empty OpenSees region is rejected at runtime).
    2. Reads the region tag the build's tag plan gave it (:meth:planned_region_tags; tag_plan must be supplied — the bridge build pipeline forwards the emit's tag plan).
    3. Emits one region $tag -node ... -ele ... line on emitter.
    4. Returns a clone with the filter selectors cleared and _region_tag populated, so the subsequent _emit appends -R $tag to the recorder command.

    Used by the flat emit path and by the stage passes. The partitioned emit path (ADR 0027 INV-4) invokes :meth:resolve_filter_ids once for each recorder of its global pass and emits the per-rank region line itself; it then injects _region_tag= onto the spec via :func:dataclasses.replace directly, bypassing this method.

    def materialize(
    self,
    emitter: "Emitter",
    fem: "FEMData",
    tag_plan: "TagPlan | None",
    fem_eid_to_ops_tag: "FemToOpsTagMap | dict[int, int] | None" = None,
) -> "FilterableRecorder":
    """Resolve filter selectors against the FEM and emit the region.

    Whole-model recording (no filter selectors) is a no-op pass-
    through.  When any of ``nodes`` / ``nodes_pg`` / ``elements`` /
    ``elements_pg`` is set, this method:

    1. Resolves ``*_pg`` to explicit id tuples via the bridge's
       PG-expansion helpers; refuses empty resolutions with
       :class:`BridgeError` (an empty OpenSees region is rejected
       at runtime).
    2. Reads the region tag the build's tag plan gave it
       (:meth:`planned_region_tags`; ``tag_plan`` must be supplied —
       the bridge build pipeline forwards the emit's tag plan).
    3. Emits one ``region $tag -node ... -ele ...`` line on
       ``emitter``.
    4. Returns a clone with the filter selectors cleared and
       ``_region_tag`` populated, so the subsequent ``_emit``
       appends ``-R $tag`` to the recorder command.

    Used by the flat emit path and by the stage passes.  The
    partitioned emit path (ADR 0027 INV-4) invokes
    :meth:`resolve_filter_ids` once for each recorder of its global
    pass and emits the per-rank region line itself; it then injects
    ``_region_tag=`` onto the spec via :func:`dataclasses.replace`
    directly, bypassing this method.
    """
    keys = self.region_keys()
    if not keys:
        return self

    from ._internal.build.errors import BridgeError

    if tag_plan is None:
        raise BridgeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} with a region (a nodes=/elements=/"
            "nodes_pg=/elements_pg= filter, or a Ladruno energy_pg=) "
            "requires a TagPlan on emit_recorder_spec(..., tag_plan=); "
            "the bridge build pipeline supplies one — tests that "
            "bypass the bridge must pass it explicitly."
        )
    return self._write_planned_regions(
        emitter, fem, self.planned_region_tags(fem, tag_plan),
        fem_eid_to_ops_tag,
    )

    MPCO dataclass ¶

    MPCO(*, file: str, nodal_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), elem_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), dT: float | None = None, nsteps: int | None = None, nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, nodes_pg: str | None = None, elements: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, elements_pg: str | None = None, _region_tag: int | None = None)

    Bases: FilterableRecorder

    recorder mpco — write a single HDF5 .mpco file.

    OpenSees command::

    recorder mpco fname.mpco [-N nodal_responses...]
                         [-E elem_responses...]
                         [-T dt $dt | -T nsteps $n]
                         [-R $regTag]

    The MPCO recorder captures the full response tensor for each requested token (no per-DOF selection at write time); STKO / apeGmsh consumers filter at read time. At least one of nodal_responses or elem_responses must be non-empty.

    Cadence is selected by exactly one of dT (seconds) or nsteps (analysis steps). Supplying both raises ValueError; supplying neither records every analysis step.

    Filtering — MPCO records the whole model by default. To restrict output to a subset of nodes/elements, supply any of nodes= / nodes_pg= / elements= / elements_pg=: the build pipeline auto-emits an OpenSees region $tag -node ... -ele ... command before the recorder and passes -R $tag to MPCO. nodes= is mutually exclusive with nodes_pg=; the same applies to the element pair. When all four are None (the default) MPCO records the whole model and no region is emitted.

    Parameters¶

    file Output .mpco (HDF5) file path. nodal_responses Tuple of MPCO -N tokens (e.g. ("displacement", "reactionForce")). Empty tuple means no nodal recording. elem_responses Tuple of MPCO -E tokens (e.g. ("stresses", "section.fiber.stress")). Empty tuple means no element recording. dT Optional time-based cadence (seconds). Mutually exclusive with nsteps. nsteps Optional step-based cadence (every N analysis steps). Mutually exclusive with dT. nodes Explicit tuple of node tags to include in the region filter. Mutually exclusive with nodes_pg. nodes_pg Physical-group label whose nodes the region filter targets. Mutually exclusive with nodes. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time. elements Explicit tuple of element tags to include in the region filter. Mutually exclusive with elements_pg. elements_pg Physical-group label whose elements the region filter targets. Mutually exclusive with elements. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time.

    Note¶

    The bridge does not interpret -R-bearing MPCO arg tails when _emit is called directly (outside the build pipeline); the pg= form is materialised by :func:apeGmsh.opensees._internal.build.recorders.emit_recorder_spec, which resolves selectors, reads its planned region tag, emits the region, and replaces the spec via :func:dataclasses.replace with explicit nodes=/elements= before driving _emit.

    Ladruno dataclass ¶

    Ladruno(*, file: str, nodal_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), elem_responses: tuple[str, ...] = (), dT: float | None = None, nsteps: int | None = None, nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, nodes_pg: str | None = None, elements: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, elements_pg: str | None = None, _region_tag: int | None = None, energy: bool = False, energy_pg: str | None = None, _energy_region_tags: tuple[int, ...] = ())

    Bases: FilterableRecorder

    recorder ladruno — write a single HDF5 .ladruno file.

    Fork-only. The ladruno recorder exists only in the Ladruno fork build of OpenSees (nmorabowen/OpenSees@ladruno); stock openseespy does not have it. Per the opt-in contract, emission works on any build (the deck line is just recorder ladruno ...); the fork requirement bites only when the deck actually runs (ops.run() / the live emitter). Gate at the point of use, never at import.

    OpenSees command (value channels + region filter + energy balance)::

    recorder ladruno fname.ladruno [-N nodal_responses...]
                               [-E elem_responses...]
                               [-T dt $dt | -T nsteps $n]
                               [-R $regTag]
                               [-G energy]

    The .ladruno recorder is forked from the frozen MPCORecorder and shares its value-channel command grammar (the -N/-E/ -T channels reproduce the frozen recorder to 1e-12), so this dataclass mirrors :class:MPCO for those channels and inherits the same region-filter machinery from :class:FilterableRecorder. It diverges only in the recorder kind token (ladruno vs mpco), the output extension (.ladruno), and the trailing -G energy channel.

    Cadence is selected by exactly one of dT (seconds) or nsteps (analysis steps). Supplying both raises ValueError; supplying neither records every analysis step.

    Filtering — like MPCO, Ladruno records the whole model by default. Supply any of nodes= / nodes_pg= / elements= / elements_pg= to restrict output: the build pipeline auto-emits an OpenSees region $tag -node ... -ele ... command before the recorder and passes -R $tag to ladruno. nodes= is mutually exclusive with nodes_pg= (same for the element pair). A node-only filter cannot be combined with elem_responses (and vice versa) — the auto-region would carry no entries on the other side and produce an empty stream. The -R $tag is emitted before -G energy so the energy flag stays last.

    energy=True adds the fork's whole-model energy-balance channel (-G energy → RESULTS/ON_DOMAIN/energyBalance, components KE/IE/DW/ULW/RES/ERR), read back via Results.energy(). The flag is emitted last: the fork's -G parser eagerly consumes trailing region-tag integers and cannot rewind past a following flag, so -G energy -T nsteps 10 is a parse error while -T nsteps 10 -G energy runs (run-verified on the fork build).

    Energy balance. Three forms, all run-verified on the fork build (which always writes the whole-model balance, RESULTS/ON_DOMAIN/energyBalance, and adds a per-region balance, RESULTS/ON_REGIONS/energyBalance, whenever a region tag is given):

    • energy=True alone → whole-model (-G energy, no tag).
    • energy=True + a value filter → energy over the same region the -R filter targets, reusing the filter's already-allocated tag (-G energy $filterTag). The coupled form.
    • energy_pg="X" → energy over an independent region X (-G energy $tagX), decoupled from the -R value filter. X may differ from (or exist without) the value-channel filter; it gets its own region tag. The decoupled form. energy_pg takes precedence over the coupled form, and implies energy recording (no need to also set energy=True).

    All three ride the flat / staged / partitioned region plumbing — the decoupled region gets its own per-rank fan-out under partitioning, just like the value filter (ADR 0064 §4). Read any region's balance via Results.energy(region=<tag>); whole-model via Results.energy().

    Parameters¶

    file Output .ladruno (HDF5) file path. nodal_responses Tuple of -N tokens (e.g. ("displacement", "reactionForce")). Empty tuple means no nodal recording. elem_responses Tuple of -E tokens (e.g. ("stresses", "section.fiber.stress")). Empty tuple means no element recording. dT Optional time-based cadence (seconds). Mutually exclusive with nsteps. nsteps Optional step-based cadence (every N analysis steps). Mutually exclusive with dT. energy Record the energy balance (-G energy). Whole-model when no filter is set; per-region (over the -R filter region, plus whole-model) when combined with a nodes=/elements= filter. energy_pg Physical-group label for a decoupled energy region — records energy over that PG (-G energy $tag) independent of the value filter. Implies energy recording. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline; gets its own auto-emitted region (per-rank under partitioning). nodes Explicit tuple of node tags for the region filter. Mutually exclusive with nodes_pg. nodes_pg Physical-group label whose nodes the region filter targets. Mutually exclusive with nodes. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time. elements Explicit tuple of element tags for the region filter. Mutually exclusive with elements_pg. elements_pg Physical-group label whose elements the region filter targets. Mutually exclusive with elements. Resolved by the bridge build pipeline at emit time.

    def resolve_energy_ids(
    self,
    fem: "FEMData",
    fem_eid_to_ops_tag: "FemToOpsTagMap | dict[int, int] | None" = None,
) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Resolve ``energy_pg`` to element ids for the energy region.

    Mirrors the element side of :meth:`resolve_filter_ids`: returns
    FEM eids verbatim when ``fem_eid_to_ops_tag is None`` (the
    partition orchestrator intersects per-rank in FEM-eid space),
    else translates to OpenSees element tags. Empty resolution →
    :class:`BridgeError`. Energy is an element quantity, so the
    region carries ``-ele`` only (the fork auto-derives the nodes).
    """
    from ._internal.build.errors import BridgeError
    from ._internal.build.pg_expand import expand_pg_to_elements

    assert self.energy_pg is not None  # caller-guarded
    fem_eids = tuple(
        eid for eid, _conn in expand_pg_to_elements(fem, self.energy_pg)
    )
    if not fem_eids:
        raise BridgeError(
            f"Ladruno energy region: energy_pg={self.energy_pg!r} "
            "resolved to zero elements against the FEM snapshot. "
            "An empty region is rejected by OpenSees at runtime; check "
            "the PG name spelling and that elements were registered "
            "against it before get_fem_data."
        )
    if fem_eid_to_ops_tag is None:
        return fem_eids
    ops_tags: list[int] = []
    for eid in fem_eids:
        ops_tag = fem_eid_to_ops_tag.get(int(eid))
        if ops_tag is None:
            raise BridgeError(
                f"Ladruno energy region: energy_pg={self.energy_pg!r} "
                f"resolves to FEM eid {eid} but no element was emitted "
                "at that eid — declare an ``ops.element.X(pg=...)`` "
                f"primitive whose pg includes {self.energy_pg!r}."
            )
        ops_tags.append(int(ops_tag))
    return tuple(ops_tags)

    def region_keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The value-filter region (base), then the decoupled energy region.

    The energy region (``energy_pg``) is independent of the ``-R``
    value filter (the fork's ``-G energy <tag>`` list is orthogonal to
    ``-R``); it takes its own tag, after the filter's.
    """
    keys = FilterableRecorder.region_keys(self)
    if self.energy_pg is not None:
        keys = (*keys, "energy")
    return keys

    Monitor dataclass ¶

    Monitor(*, sink: str, dofs: tuple[int, ...], nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, pg: str | None = None, resp: str = 'disp', every: int | None = None, hz: float | None = None)

    Bases: Recorder

    recorder Monitor — live SWMR-HDF5 nodal-telemetry sink (fork-only).

    Fork-only. The Monitor recorder exists only in the Ladruno fork build; stock openseespy does not have it. Emission works on any build (the deck line is just recorder Monitor ...); the fork requirement bites only when the deck runs. Gate at the point of use.

    Unlike the canonical :class:Ladruno recorder, the Monitor is a lightweight live-telemetry sidecar: it streams a few selected nodal scalars to a small SWMR-HDF5 file a viewer process can tail while the analysis is still running. The same file is a valid at-rest result once the run finishes — read both via :func:apeGmsh.results.read_monitor / :func:apeGmsh.results.tail_monitor.

    OpenSees command::

    recorder Monitor (-node n1 n2 ... | -region tag) -dof d1 d2 ...
                 [-resp disp|vel|accel|reaction]
                 -sink fname.h5 [-every K] [-hz H]

    Exactly one of nodes= (explicit tags) or pg= (physical-group label, resolved against the FEM snapshot by the bridge build pipeline) must be supplied. The recorded channels are the cartesian product of nodes × dofs, labelled node<N>.<resp>.dof<D> in node-major order.

    Parameters¶

    sink Output .h5 SWMR sink path. dofs DOF indices (1-based, OpenSees convention). At least one required. nodes Explicit tuple of node tags. Mutually exclusive with pg. pg Physical-group label whose nodes are monitored. Mutually exclusive with nodes; resolved at emit time. resp Nodal response — one of disp / vel / accel / reaction (the fork v1 set). Default disp. every Step decimation — emit a frame every K analysis steps. None records every step. hz Wall-clock throttle — emit at most H frames per second of real time (the first frame always passes). None means no throttle. Independent of every; both may bound the stream.

    RecorderRecord dataclass ¶

    RecorderRecord(*, category: str, components: tuple[str, ...] = (), raw: tuple[str, ...] = (), pg: tuple[str, ...] = (), label: tuple[str, ...] = (), selection: tuple[str, ...] = (), ids: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, dt: float | None = None, n_steps: int | None = None, name: str | None = None, n_modes: int | None = None, element_class_name: str | None = None)

    One category-level declaration entry within a RecorderDeclaration.

    Stores already-expanded canonical components (or raw OpenSees tokens via the raw= escape hatch). Shorthand expansion ("displacement" → displacement_x/y/z) happens at construction in the namespace method (Phase 9 commit 3), not in this dataclass — by the time a record is built, components are fully expanded.

    Parameters¶

    category One of :data:ALL_RECORDER_CATEGORIES. components Tuple of canonical component names, each one the category records (:func:apeGmsh._vocabulary.in_category: the CATEGORY_COMPONENTS table plus its indexed canonicals, state_variable_<n>, fiber_stress_<n>, spring_force_<n>). A bare string is one component. raw Escape hatch for non-canonical OpenSees tokens (e.g. a custom recorder response). Bypasses canonical validation. pg / label / selection / ids Target selectors. ids= is mutually exclusive with the named selectors. Resolution against FEMData happens at emit time (commit 3). dt / n_steps Recording cadence. At most one may be set; both None records every step. name Optional user-supplied name for this record; auto-generated when None. n_modes Required for category="modal"; rejected for other categories. element_class_name Optional OpenSees C++ class name override for element-level records. Used by the .out transcoder to disambiguate elements that share a flat response size (e.g. tri31 vs SSPquad). Carried from the legacy Recorders.elements contract.

    RecorderDeclaration(*, records: tuple[RecorderRecord, ...], name: str = 'default', ndm: int = 3, ndf: int = 6, file_root: str = '.')

    Bases: Recorder

    A bundle of recorder records, registered as a single Primitive.

    Captures the bridge's ndm and ndf at construction time (Phase 9 D8 — implicit source-of-truth binding). Drives the file-emit path via :func:emit_recorder_spec in :mod:apeGmsh.opensees._internal.build.

    Parameters¶

    records Tuple of :class:RecorderRecord entries. Each is one category-level declaration; emit fans them out into one or more concrete OpenSees recorder commands. name Identifier for this declaration (defaults to "default"). Multiple named declarations can coexist on one bridge. ndm, ndf Snapshot of the bridge's ndm/ndf at construction time. Used downstream for shorthand expansion and validation. The bridge passes these in (Phase 9 D8 — user never repeats ops.model(ndm=, ndf=) values). file_root Directory prefix for emitted .out files. Each record fans out to <file_root>/<decl.name>__<record_name>__<token>.out. Defaults to "." (current working directory).

    def build_recorder_declaration(
    *,
    ndm: int,
    ndf: int,
    nodes: "Iterable[str] | str" = (),
    elements: "Iterable[str] | str" = (),
    line_stations: "Iterable[str] | str" = (),
    gauss: "Iterable[str] | str" = (),
    raw_nodes: "Iterable[str] | str | None" = None,
    raw_elements: "Iterable[str] | str | None" = None,
    raw_line_stations: "Iterable[str] | str | None" = None,
    raw_gauss: "Iterable[str] | str | None" = None,
    pg: "str | Iterable[str] | None" = None,
    label: "str | Iterable[str] | None" = None,
    selection: "str | Iterable[str] | None" = None,
    ids: "Iterable[int] | None" = None,
    dt: float | None = None,
    n_steps: int | None = None,
    name: str = "default",
    record_name: str | None = None,
    element_class_name: str | None = None,
    file_root: str = ".",
) -> RecorderDeclaration:
    """Construct a :class:`RecorderDeclaration` from declarative kwargs.

    Single source of truth for shorthand expansion (``"displacement"``
    → ``displacement_x/y/z`` via the bound ``ndm``/``ndf``) and
    per-category record construction.  Shared by
    :meth:`apeGmsh.opensees._internal.ns.recorder._RecorderNS.declare`
    (bridge-owned models) and
    :meth:`apeGmsh.opensees.ModelData.recorders` (hand-written decks).

    ``ndm`` / ``ndf`` are supplied by the caller (the bridge or
    ``ModelData`` binds them at declaration time, Phase 9 D8 — the user
    never repeats ``ndm=``/``ndf=`` here).
    """
    pg_tuple = _normalize_str_selector(pg)
    label_tuple = _normalize_str_selector(label)
    selection_tuple = _normalize_str_selector(selection)
    ids_tuple = tuple(int(i) for i in ids) if ids is not None else None

    records: list[RecorderRecord] = []

    # Per-category record construction. Each category produces at most
    # one record (canonical components + raw tokens combined). A record
    # is skipped only when both are empty for that category.
    category_inputs: tuple[
        tuple[str, "Iterable[str] | str", "Iterable[str] | str | None"], ...
    ] = (
        ("nodes",         nodes,         raw_nodes),
        ("elements",      elements,      raw_elements),
        ("line_stations", line_stations, raw_line_stations),
        ("gauss",         gauss,         raw_gauss),
    )
    for category, canonical_kw, raw_kw in category_inputs:
        canonical_seq = _normalize_str_selector(canonical_kw)
        raw_seq = _normalize_str_selector(raw_kw)
        if not canonical_seq and not raw_seq:
            continue
        components = (
            expand_many(canonical_seq, ndm=ndm, ndf=ndf)
            if canonical_seq else ()
        )
        records.append(
            RecorderRecord(
                category=category,
                components=components,
                raw=raw_seq,
                pg=pg_tuple,
                label=label_tuple,
                selection=selection_tuple,
                ids=ids_tuple,
                dt=dt,
                n_steps=n_steps,
                name=record_name,
                element_class_name=(
                    element_class_name if category != "nodes" else None
                ),
            )
        )

    return RecorderDeclaration(
        records=tuple(records),
        name=name,
        ndm=ndm,
        ndf=ndf,
        file_root=file_root,
    )

    Building tables¶

    Story forces, story drifts, pier forces and story masses (the ETABS Story Forces, Story Drifts, Pier Forces and Mass Summary by Story tables), read in-process from the live domain. The extractor classes are callables extractor(ops) -> ndarray with a labels tuple, so a modal driver can evaluate them at each mode.

    apeGmsh.opensees.building ¶

    Story and pier aggregation on the live OpenSees domain.

    The building tables an ETABS model reports — Story Forces, Story Drifts, Pier Forces and Mass Summary by Story / Centers of Mass — computed in-process from the domain the bridge built (:func:~apeGmsh.opensees.emitter.live.get_ops, or an explicit ops=).

    Every quantity is read from the current domain state, so the same object serves a static case, the gravity state of a P-Delta run, and each mode of a response-spectrum analysis.

    Extractors¶

    :class:StoryForces, :class:StoryDrifts and :class:PierForces are extractors: callables extractor(ops) -> ndarray of a fixed length, with a matching labels tuple (the :class:Extractor protocol). The domain is scanned once, at construction (node coordinates, element connectivity, the elements and nodes each cut needs, the checks below); a call only reads element forces and node displacements for those, both at the trial state (eleForce is the trial resisting force; a displacement is nodeDisp, the committed value, plus nodeResponse IncrDisp, trial minus committed). After a committed solve the two states agree; an uncommitted trial state, such as gravity plus one mode left by responseSpectrumAnalysis -increment, is read as is. A modal driver evaluates an extractor at each mode and combines each entry of the vector across modes; :meth:StoryForces.table (and the other table methods) reshapes any such vector, combined or not, into a :class:StoryTable. The plain functions :func:story_forces, :func:story_drifts, :func:pier_forces and :func:story_masses are the one-off forms.

    The free body¶

    A story or pier force is the resultant the part above a horizontal cut transmits to the part below. The cut is node-aligned: it runs through the nodes at the cut elevation, and an element belongs to the part above when all its nodes are at or above the cut and it does not lie in the cut plane. Elements in the plane (the floor slab, the level's beams) belong to the part below; nodal loads on cut nodes act on the part below. eleForce (the forces response: Element::getResistingForce, the global nodal force vector the integrator assembles, element loads included) of the elements above that touch the cut gives, at each cut node, the force the node applies to them; the force they transmit is its negative. Hence, for a structure loaded only above the cut,

    ``(VX, VY, P) = sum of the loads applied above the cut``

    exactly (to solver round-off), and at the base it equals -sum(R) (:func:base_shear_from_reactions). Negate the six components for the reaction convention. The top of a story (location="top") is the cut just below a level, read from the elements below it that touch the level.

    Refusals¶

    • an element whose nodes lie strictly on both sides of a cut (the cut is not node-aligned there);
    • an MP constraint (rigid link, equalDOF, ...) joining a node of the part above to a node of the part below: it carries force past the elements, so the element free body would miss it;
    • any EQ constraint in the domain (equationConstraint, the fork's LadrunoTie): OpenSees does not report their nodes, so whether one crosses a cut cannot be checked. The count comes from a printModel dump to a temporary file, which :class:StoryForces writes once, at construction, never per call. It costs about 30 µs per node and element on a fresh domain, and up to ~150 µs once eigen has run, because Node::Print then writes every eigenvector (16.6 s and 42 MB for 10k shells after eigen(50)): build the extractor before eigen, once, and evaluate it at every mode;
    • in :class:StoryDrifts joint mode, a node on a level with no node at the same plan position on the level below (a cantilever tip, a transfer level, an offset column), named; dropping it would hide its drift;
    • an element whose forces vector is not one value per DOF of its nodes (eleType is named);
    • nodes with an ndf other than 3 or 6, and 2-D models.

    Code checks¶

    The tables carry what an ASCE 7 check reads; naming columns is the caller's. AvgX / AvgY are the ASCE 7-22 average of the signed values at the two ends of the structure (Table 12.3-1, Types 1a/1b; delta_avg of Eq. 12.8-14), |d_A + d_B| / 2, the ends being the entries farthest apart across the direction (:func:_max_avg). It is not a mean over every joint, so the max/avg ratio and Ax do not move with the mesh. For example, apeETABS's TorsionCheck drifts frame::

    t = drifts.story_max(combined).to_frame().rename_axis("Story").reset_index()
h = dict(zip(drifts.stories, drifts.heights))
t["Elevation"] = list(drifts.levels[1:])
t["drift_max"] = t["DriftX"] * t["Story"].map(h)
t["drift_avg"] = t["AvgX"] * t["Story"].map(h)

    and its displacements frame (for Ax) is StoryDisplacements.story_max() with MaxX, AvgX renamed Maximum, Average.

    Story shear and overturning per story, as an :class:Extractor.

    Parameters¶

    levels Level elevations, strictly increasing, the base first. Story i (i = 1..n) spans levels[i-1] to levels[i] and is named after its top level. names One name per level (default "Base", "Story1", ...). location "bottom" (default): the cut just above levels[i-1], the resultant of every load above that level. "top": the cut just below levels[i], the resultant of every load at or above it. reference Plan point (x, y) the moments are taken about, at each cut's elevation (default the origin). MZ is the story torsion. ops The OpenSees module; default :func:~apeGmsh.opensees.emitter.live.get_ops. tol Elevation tolerance; default 1e-6 of the model's size.

    A call returns [VX, VY, P, MX, MY, MZ] per story, stories in level order (labels names each entry "<story>:<component>").

    Construction checks the domain for EQ constraints with one printModel dump (see Refusals); a call does not repeat it. Build the extractor before eigen (the dump then omits eigenvectors) and evaluate the same object at every mode.

    def __init__(
    self,
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    location: Literal["bottom", "top"] = "bottom",
    reference: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0),
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    where = "StoryForces"
    if location not in ("bottom", "top"):
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: location must be 'bottom' or 'top', "
                         f"got {location!r}.")
    z = _check_levels(levels, where)
    level_names = _level_names(names, z.size, where)
    self.levels: tuple[float, ...] = tuple(float(v) for v in z)
    self.stories: tuple[str, ...] = level_names[1:]
    self.location = location
    self._ref_xy = (float(reference[0]), float(reference[1]))
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    self._dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    n_eq = _eq_constraint_count(module, where)
    if n_eq:
        raise BridgeError(
            f"{where}: the domain holds {n_eq} EQ constraint(s) "
            "(equationConstraint, LadrunoTie, or an enforce='equation' "
            "tie). OpenSees does not report their nodes, so a cut "
            "cannot tell whether one carries force past the elements, "
            "which the element free body would miss. Story forces "
            "refuse any EQ constraint; tie with equalDOF / rigid links "
            "inside a level, or read the forces from a model without them."
        )
    mp = _mp_pairs(module, self._dom)
    self._gather = _Gatherer()
    cuts: list[_Cut] = []
    for i in range(1, z.size):
        if location == "bottom":
            cuts.append(_build_cut(module, self._dom, self._gather, z[i - 1],
                                   "above", None, f"{where} {self.stories[i-1]}",
                                   check_mp=mp))
        else:
            cuts.append(_build_cut(module, self._dom, self._gather, z[i],
                                   "below", None, f"{where} {self.stories[i-1]}",
                                   check_mp=mp))
    self._gather.freeze()
    self._cuts = tuple(cuts)
    self.labels: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(
        f"{s}:{c}" for s in self.stories for c in STORY_FORCE_COMPONENTS)

    def table(self, values: FloatArray | None = None, *,
          ops: ModuleType | None = None) -> StoryTable:
    """``values`` (a call's vector, or any combination of them) as a
    story × component table; evaluates now when ``values`` is ``None``."""
    v = self(ops) if values is None else _check_len(values, self.labels)
    return StoryTable(self.stories, STORY_FORCE_COMPONENTS,
                      v.reshape(len(self.stories), 6))

    StoryDrifts(levels: Sequence[float], *, points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] | None = None, names: Sequence[str] | None = None, method: Literal['nearest', 'rigid'] = 'nearest', max_offset: float | None = None, ops: ModuleType | None = None, tol: float | None = None)

    Parameters¶

    levels, names, ops, tol As :class:StoryForces. points Plan points (x, y) to report. None (default) reports every joint: each node at a level that has a node at the same plan position (within tol) on the level below — ETABS Joint Drifts, whose maximum per story (:meth:story_max) is ETABS Story Drifts. A node on a level above the base with no node at its plan position on the level below raises, named (its drift would otherwise be left out). method How a point reads a level's displacement. "nearest": the nearest node of the level in plan, which must lie within max_offset (default tol). "rigid": the least-squares in-plane rigid motion (ux, uy, rz) of all the level's nodes, evaluated at the point (exact for a rigid diaphragm).

    A call returns [DX, DY] per entry, entries per story in level order; labels reads "<story>:<node>:DX" (joints) or "<story>:P<j>:DX" (points). Displacements are the trial displacements (see the module notes).

    def __init__(
    self,
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] | None = None,
    names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    method: Literal["nearest", "rigid"] = "nearest",
    max_offset: float | None = None,
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    where = "StoryDrifts"
    if method not in ("nearest", "rigid"):
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: method must be 'nearest' or 'rigid', "
                         f"got {method!r}.")
    z = _check_levels(levels, where)
    level_names = _level_names(names, z.size, where)
    self.levels: tuple[float, ...] = tuple(float(v) for v in z)
    self.stories: tuple[str, ...] = level_names[1:]
    self.heights: tuple[float, ...] = tuple(float(h) for h in np.diff(z))
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    self._dom = dom
    on_level = [np.flatnonzero(np.abs(dom.coords[:, 2] - zk) <= dom.tol)
                for zk in z]
    for k, rows in enumerate(on_level):
        if rows.size == 0:
            raise BridgeError(f"{where}: no node lies on level "
                              f"{level_names[k]!r} (z={z[k]:g}).")
    # Each entry: (story index, top operator, bottom operator); an
    # operator maps the level's needed node displacements to (ux, uy).
    self._story: list[int] = []
    self._ops_top: list[tuple[IntArray, FloatArray]] = []
    self._ops_bot: list[tuple[IntArray, FloatArray]] = []
    self._xy: list[FloatArray] = []          # plan point of each entry
    labels: list[str] = []
    if points is None:
        for i in range(1, z.size):
            top, bot = on_level[i], on_level[i - 1]
            d = np.linalg.norm(dom.coords[top, None, :2]
                               - dom.coords[None, bot, :2], axis=2)
            b_of = np.argmin(d, axis=1)
            lone = top[d[np.arange(top.size), b_of] > dom.tol]
            if lone.size:
                tags = [int(t) for t in dom.node_tags[lone[:8]]]
                raise BridgeError(
                    f"{where}: story {self.stories[i-1]!r}: node(s) {tags}"
                    f"{' ...' if lone.size > 8 else ''} of level "
                    f"{level_names[i]!r} (z={z[i]:g}) have no node at the "
                    f"same plan position on level {level_names[i-1]!r} "
                    f"(z={z[i-1]:g}), as at a cantilever tip, a transfer "
                    "level or an offset column. Dropping them would hide "
                    "their drift; pass points= (method='rigid' for a "
                    "rigid diaphragm)."
                )
            for a, row in enumerate(top):
                self._add(i - 1, _pick(int(row)), _pick(int(bot[int(b_of[a])])),
                          dom.coords[row, :2])
                tag = int(dom.node_tags[row])
                labels += [f"{self.stories[i-1]}:{tag}:DX",
                           f"{self.stories[i-1]}:{tag}:DY"]
    else:
        pts = [(float(p[0]), float(p[1])) for p in points]
        if not pts:
            raise ValueError(f"{where}: points is empty; pass None for every joint.")
        off = dom.tol if max_offset is None else float(max_offset)
        per_level: list[list[tuple[IntArray, FloatArray]]] = []
        for k, rows in enumerate(on_level):
            if method == "nearest":
                per_level.append([
                    _nearest(dom, rows, p, off, f"{where} level "
                             f"{level_names[k]!r}") for p in pts])
            else:
                per_level.append(_rigid(dom, rows, pts,
                                        f"{where} level {level_names[k]!r}"))
        for i in range(1, z.size):
            for j in range(len(pts)):
                self._add(i - 1, per_level[i][j], per_level[i - 1][j],
                          np.asarray(pts[j]))
                labels += [f"{self.stories[i-1]}:P{j}:DX",
                           f"{self.stories[i-1]}:P{j}:DY"]
    need = sorted({int(r) for op in self._ops_top + self._ops_bot for r in op[0]})
    self._need = np.asarray(need, dtype=np.int64)
    pos = {r: k for k, r in enumerate(need)}
    self._top_idx = [np.asarray([pos[int(r)] for r in op[0]], dtype=np.int64)
                     for op in self._ops_top]
    self._bot_idx = [np.asarray([pos[int(r)] for r in op[0]], dtype=np.int64)
                     for op in self._ops_bot]
    self._h = np.asarray([self.heights[s] for s in self._story])
    self._xy_arr = np.asarray(self._xy, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 2)
    self.labels: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(labels)

    def __init__(
    self,
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] | None = None,
    names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    method: Literal["nearest", "rigid"] = "nearest",
    max_offset: float | None = None,
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    where = "StoryDisplacements"
    if method not in ("nearest", "rigid"):
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: method must be 'nearest' or 'rigid', "
                         f"got {method!r}.")
    z = _check_levels(levels, where)
    level_names = _level_names(names, z.size, where)
    self.levels: tuple[float, ...] = tuple(float(v) for v in z)
    self.stories: tuple[str, ...] = level_names[1:]
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    self._dom = dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    self._story: list[int] = []
    self._ops: list[tuple[IntArray, FloatArray]] = []
    self._xy: list[FloatArray] = []          # plan point of each entry
    labels: list[str] = []
    for i in range(1, z.size):
        w = f"{where} level {level_names[i]!r}"
        rows = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(dom.coords[:, 2] - z[i]) <= dom.tol)
        if rows.size == 0:
            raise BridgeError(f"{w}: no node lies on it (z={z[i]:g}).")
        if points is None:
            ops_i = [_pick(int(r)) for r in rows]
            keys = [str(int(dom.node_tags[r])) for r in rows]
            xy_i = [dom.coords[r, :2] for r in rows]
        else:
            pts = [(float(p[0]), float(p[1])) for p in points]
            off = dom.tol if max_offset is None else float(max_offset)
            ops_i = ([_nearest(dom, rows, p, off, w) for p in pts]
                     if method == "nearest" else _rigid(dom, rows, pts, w))
            keys = [f"P{j}" for j in range(len(pts))]
            xy_i = [np.asarray(p) for p in pts]
        for op, key, xy in zip(ops_i, keys, xy_i):
            self._story.append(i - 1)
            self._ops.append(op)
            self._xy.append(xy)
            labels += [f"{level_names[i]}:{key}:UX", f"{level_names[i]}:{key}:UY"]
    self._xy_arr = np.asarray(self._xy, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 2)
    self.labels: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(labels)

    @classmethod
def from_pg(
    cls,
    bridge: "apeSees",
    pg: str,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    bottom: float | None = None,
    top: float | None = None,
    axis2: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
) -> "Pier":
    """The pier of physical group ``pg``'s elements in ``bridge``.

    FEM element ids map to OpenSees tags directly under
    ``element_tags="fem"``; otherwise through the bridge's live read
    session (after a live ``analyze``), which raises when there is none.
    """
    from ._readback import live_session

    where = f"Pier.from_pg({pg!r})"
    ids = [int(e) for e in bridge.fem.elements.select(pg=pg).ids]
    if not ids:
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: the physical group has no elements.")
    if bridge._element_tags == "fem":
        tags = tuple(ids)
    else:
        rows = live_session(bridge, where).element_rows(ids, where)
        tags = tuple(t for _spec, t in rows)
    return cls(name=pg if name is None else name, elements=tags,
               bottom=bottom, top=top, axis2=axis2)

    Pier forces at the bottom and top of each pier, as an :class:Extractor.

    P, V2, V3, T, M2, M3 in pier local axes (axis 1 up, axis 2 along the pier in plan, axis 3 = 1 × 2), moments about the centroid of the pier section at the cut (the length-weighted centroid of the element edges on the cut, which assumes a uniform thickness). Both cuts give the force the part above transmits to the part below, so P is negative in compression and, under a lateral load H along axis 2 at height L above the cut, V2 = H and M3 = H L.

    def __init__(
    self,
    piers: Sequence[Pier],
    *,
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    where = "PierForces"
    self.piers: tuple[Pier, ...] = tuple(piers)
    if not self.piers:
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: piers is empty.")
    names = [p.name for p in self.piers]
    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: pier names must be unique; got {names}.")
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    self._dom = dom
    self._gather = _Gatherer()
    cuts: list[_PierCuts] = []
    for p in self.piers:
        w = f"{where} {p.name!r}"
        idx = _element_index(dom, p, w)
        zb = float(dom.ele_zmin[idx].min()) if p.bottom is None else float(p.bottom)
        zt = float(dom.ele_zmax[idx].max()) if p.top is None else float(p.top)
        if not zt > zb + dom.tol:
            raise ValueError(f"{w}: top ({zt:g}) must lie above bottom ({zb:g}).")
        outside = idx[(dom.ele_zmin[idx] < zb - dom.tol)
                      | (dom.ele_zmax[idx] > zt + dom.tol)]
        if outside.size:
            bad = [int(dom.ele_tags[k]) for k in outside[:8]]
            raise BridgeError(
                f"{w}: element(s) {bad} reach outside the pier's cuts "
                f"(z {zb:g} to {zt:g}); split a multi-story pier with "
                "piers_by_story()."
            )
        bot = _build_cut(module, dom, self._gather, zb, "above", idx, w,
                         check_mp=None)
        top = _build_cut(module, dom, self._gather, zt, "below", idx, w,
                         check_mp=None)
        axes = _pier_axes(dom, bot, p.axis2, w)
        cuts.append(_PierCuts(bot, top, axes, _section_centroid(dom, bot, zb),
                              _section_centroid(dom, top, zt)))
    self._gather.freeze()
    self._cuts = tuple(cuts)
    self.labels: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(
        f"{p.name}:{loc}:{c}" for p in self.piers for loc in ("bottom", "top")
        for c in PIER_FORCE_COMPONENTS)

    def base_shear_from_reactions(
    z_base: float,
    *,
    reference: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0),
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> FloatArray:
    """``-sum(R)`` over the nodes at or below ``z_base``, as
    ``[VX, VY, P, MX, MY, MZ]`` about ``(reference, z_base)``.

    The cross-check of the base story's :class:`StoryForces` row: the two
    agree when no load is applied at or below the base. Calls
    ``ops.reactions()``.
    """
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    dom = _capture(module, tol, "base_shear_from_reactions")
    module.reactions()
    ref = np.array([float(reference[0]), float(reference[1]), float(z_base)])
    force = np.zeros(3)
    moment = np.zeros(3)
    for r in np.flatnonzero(dom.coords[:, 2] <= float(z_base) + dom.tol):
        reac = np.asarray(module.nodeReaction(int(dom.node_tags[r])), dtype=np.float64)
        f = reac[:3]
        force += f
        moment += np.cross(dom.coords[r] - ref, f)
        if reac.size >= 6:
            moment += reac[3:6]
    return np.asarray(-np.concatenate([force, moment]), dtype=np.float64)

    def piers_by_story(
    pier: Pier,
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[Pier, ...]:
    """Split ``pier`` (one PG over many stories) into one pier per story.

    Each story's pier holds the elements between its two levels and is
    named ``"<pier>/<story>"``; a story with none is left out. An element
    that crosses a level raises.
    """
    where = f"piers_by_story({pier.name!r})"
    z = _check_levels(levels, where)
    level_names = _level_names(names, z.size, where)
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    idx = _element_index(dom, pier, where)
    out: list[Pier] = []
    assigned = np.zeros(idx.size, dtype=bool)
    for i in range(1, z.size):
        sel = ((dom.ele_zmin[idx] >= z[i - 1] - dom.tol)
               & (dom.ele_zmax[idx] <= z[i] + dom.tol))
        assigned |= sel
        if sel.any():
            out.append(Pier(
                name=f"{pier.name}/{level_names[i]}",
                elements=tuple(int(dom.ele_tags[k]) for k in idx[sel]),
                bottom=float(z[i - 1]), top=float(z[i]), axis2=pier.axis2))
    if not assigned.all():
        bad = [int(dom.ele_tags[k]) for k in idx[~assigned][:8]]
        raise BridgeError(f"{where}: element(s) {bad} do not lie between two "
                          "consecutive levels (they cross a level, or lie "
                          "outside the levels).")
    return tuple(out)

A node on a level goes to that level; a node between two levels is split between them linearly in height (a lumped story element's mass goes half to each level); a node at or below the base goes to the base row, one above the top level to the top row.     def story_masses(
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    include_elements: bool = True,
    ops: ModuleType | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> StoryTable:
    """Translational mass and center of mass per level (ETABS *Mass
    Summary by Story* / *Centers of Mass*).

    Rows are the level names (the base first); columns ``MassX, MassY,
    MassZ, XCM, YCM``. A node's mass is the nodal ``mass`` (``nodeMass``)
    plus, with ``include_elements``, what the elements lump to it (see
    :func:`_element_translational_mass`: element ``rho``, frame mass per
    length, shell ``rho * h``, whatever the build defines). A node on a
    level goes to that level; a node between two levels is split between
    them linearly in height (a lumped story element's mass goes half to
    each level); a node at or below the base goes to the base row, one
    above the top level to the top row. ``XCM, YCM`` weigh the horizontal
    mass ``(MassX + MassY) / 2``. ``modalProperties`` counts only free
    DOFs, so with a fixed base its total mass is the sum of the rows above
    the base.
    """
    where = "story_masses"
    z = _check_levels(levels, where)
    level_names = _level_names(names, z.size, where)
    module = _resolve_ops(ops)
    dom = _capture(module, tol, where)
    m = np.zeros((dom.node_tags.size, 3))
    for r, t in enumerate(dom.node_tags):
        nm = np.asarray(module.nodeMass(int(t)), dtype=np.float64).ravel()
        k = min(3, nm.size)
        m[r, :k] = nm[:k]
    if include_elements:
        m += _element_translational_mass(module, dom)
    nz = dom.coords[:, 2]
    w = np.zeros((dom.node_tags.size, z.size))     # node -> level weights
    for r in range(dom.node_tags.size):
        zr = nz[r]
        if zr <= z[0] + dom.tol:
            w[r, 0] = 1.0
        elif zr >= z[-1] - dom.tol:
            w[r, -1] = 1.0
        else:
            i = int(np.searchsorted(z, zr))
            if abs(zr - z[i - 1]) <= dom.tol:
                w[r, i - 1] = 1.0
            elif abs(zr - z[i]) <= dom.tol:
                w[r, i] = 1.0
            else:
                t = (zr - z[i - 1]) / (z[i] - z[i - 1])
                w[r, i - 1] = 1.0 - t
                w[r, i] = t
    mass = w.T @ m                                    # (L, 3)
    mh = 0.5 * (m[:, 0] + m[:, 1])
    wh = w.T @ mh
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        xcm = np.where(wh > 0.0, (w.T @ (mh * dom.coords[:, 0])) / wh, np.nan)
        ycm = np.where(wh > 0.0, (w.T @ (mh * dom.coords[:, 1])) / wh, np.nan)
    return StoryTable(level_names, STORY_MASS_COLUMNS,
                      np.column_stack([mass, xcm, ycm]))

    def levels_from_pgs(
    fem: "FEMData",
    pgs: Sequence[str],
    *,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """The elevation of each physical group in ``pgs`` (one per level).

    Every node of a group must lie at one elevation within ``tol``
    (default ``1e-6`` of the model's size); the result keeps ``pgs``'s
    order, which must be strictly increasing.
    """
    where = "levels_from_pgs"
    if tol is None:
        all_xyz = np.asarray(fem.nodes.coords, dtype=np.float64)
        span = float(np.linalg.norm(all_xyz.max(axis=0) - all_xyz.min(axis=0)))
        tol = 1e-6 * max(span, 1.0)
    out: list[float] = []
    for name in pgs:
        xyz = np.asarray(fem.nodes.select(pg=name).coords, dtype=np.float64)
        if xyz.size == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{where}: physical group {name!r} has no nodes.")
        zs = xyz.reshape(-1, 3)[:, 2]
        if float(zs.max() - zs.min()) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where}: physical group {name!r} spans z {zs.min():g} to "
                f"{zs.max():g}; a level group must be horizontal (tol {tol:g})."
            )
        out.append(float(zs.mean()))
    _check_levels(out, where)
    return tuple(out)

    def renumber(
    self,
    method: str = "simple",
    *,
    base: int = 1,
    used_only: bool = True,
) -> NumberedMesh:
    """
    Produce a solver-ready mesh with contiguous IDs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method : ``"simple"`` or ``"rcm"``
        ``"simple"``  — preserves relative order, just makes IDs
        contiguous.  Fast, no optimisation.

        ``"rcm"``  — Reverse Cuthill-McKee bandwidth minimisation.
        Reorders nodes so that the assembled stiffness matrix has
        minimal bandwidth.  Recommended for direct solvers.

    base : int
        Starting ID (default 1 = Fortran/OpenSees convention;
        use 0 for C/Python convention).

    used_only : bool
        If True (default), only include nodes that appear in at
        least one element (skip orphan nodes).  Set False to
        include all nodes from the mesh.

    Returns
    -------
    NumberedMesh
    """
    # ── Filter nodes ──────────────────────────────────────────
    if used_only:
        mask = np.isin(self._node_tags, list(self._used_tags))
        n_total   = len(self._node_tags)
        gmsh_tags = self._node_tags[mask]
        coords    = self._node_coords[mask]
        n_orphans = n_total - len(gmsh_tags)
        if n_orphans > 0:
            orphan_tags = self._node_tags[~mask]
            print(
                f"[Numberer] WARNING: {n_orphans} orphan node(s) "
                f"skipped (not connected to any element). "
                f"Tags: {orphan_tags.tolist()[:20]}"
                + (f" ... (+{n_orphans - 20} more)"
                   if n_orphans > 20 else "")
            )
    else:
        gmsh_tags = self._node_tags.copy()
        coords    = self._node_coords.copy()

    n_nodes = len(gmsh_tags)

    # ── Temporary 0-based indexing ────────────────────────────
    # Map Gmsh tags -> 0-based indices for internal work
    gtag_to_tmp: dict[int, int] = {
        int(t): i for i, t in enumerate(gmsh_tags)
    }

    # Rewrite connectivity in 0-based tmp indices (vectorized)
    flat = self._connectivity.ravel()
    conn_tmp = np.array(
        [gtag_to_tmp[int(t)] for t in flat],
        dtype=int,
    ).reshape(self._connectivity.shape)

    # ── Compute permutation ───────────────────────────────────
    if method == "rcm":
        perm = _rcm_ordering(n_nodes, conn_tmp)
    elif method == "simple":
        perm = np.arange(n_nodes, dtype=int)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown method '{method}'. Use 'simple' or 'rcm'."
        )

    # perm[new_pos] = old_pos
    # inverse: inv_perm[old_pos] = new_pos
    inv_perm = np.empty(n_nodes, dtype=int)
    inv_perm[perm] = np.arange(n_nodes)

    # ── Apply permutation ─────────────────────────────────────
    new_coords     = coords[perm]            # reordered coords

    # Rewrite connectivity with new IDs (vectorized)
    new_conn = inv_perm[conn_tmp] + base

    # Element IDs: simple contiguous
    new_elem_ids = np.arange(base, base + len(self._elem_tags), dtype=int)

    # ── Bandwidth ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    bw = _compute_bandwidth(new_conn)

    # ── Build maps ────────────────────────────────────────────
    g2s_node: dict[int, int] = {}
    s2g_node: dict[int, int] = {}
    for new_pos in range(n_nodes):
        old_pos = perm[new_pos]
        gtag = int(gmsh_tags[old_pos])
        sid  = int(inv_perm[old_pos]) + base
        g2s_node[gtag] = sid
        s2g_node[sid]  = gtag

    g2s_elem: dict[int, int] = {}
    s2g_elem: dict[int, int] = {}
    for i, etag in enumerate(self._elem_tags):
        eid = int(new_elem_ids[i])
        g2s_elem[int(etag)] = eid
        s2g_elem[eid]       = int(etag)

    # ── Rewrite node_ids array in order ───────────────────────
    # node_ids[i] = solver ID of the i-th node (in new ordering)
    solver_node_ids = np.arange(base, base + n_nodes, dtype=int)

    result = NumberedMesh(
        node_ids=solver_node_ids,
        node_coords=new_coords,
        elem_ids=new_elem_ids,
        connectivity=new_conn,
        n_nodes=n_nodes,
        n_elems=len(self._elem_tags),
        bandwidth=bw,
        method=method,
        gmsh_to_solver_node=g2s_node,
        solver_to_gmsh_node=s2g_node,
        gmsh_to_solver_elem=g2s_elem,
        solver_to_gmsh_elem=s2g_elem,
    )

    return result

    def compare_methods(self) -> dict[str, int]:
    """
    Compare bandwidth for all available methods.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, int]
        ``{"simple": bw1, "rcm": bw2}``
    """
    results = {}
    for method in ("simple", "rcm"):
        data = self.renumber(method=method)
        results[method] = data.bandwidth
    return results

    NumberedMesh(node_ids: ndarray, node_coords: ndarray, elem_ids: ndarray, connectivity: ndarray, n_nodes: int = 0, n_elems: int = 0, bandwidth: int = 0, method: str = 'simple', gmsh_to_solver_node: dict[int, int] = dict(), solver_to_gmsh_node: dict[int, int] = dict(), gmsh_to_solver_elem: dict[int, int] = dict(), solver_to_gmsh_elem: dict[int, int] = dict())

    Solver-ready mesh with contiguous IDs and bidirectional maps.

    All IDs are 1-based (the standard in structural FEM solvers like OpenSees, Abaqus, SAP2000). Set base=0 in :meth:Numberer.renumber for 0-based if your solver needs it.

    Attributes¶

    node_ids : ndarray(N,) New contiguous node IDs. node_coords : ndarray(N, 3) Nodal coordinates, same order as node_ids. elem_ids : ndarray(E,) New contiguous element IDs. connectivity : ndarray(E, npe) Element connectivity in terms of new node IDs. n_nodes : int n_elems : int bandwidth : int Semi-bandwidth of the resulting adjacency. method : str Numbering method used ("simple" or "rcm").

    Maps ~~~~ gmsh_to_solver_node : dict[int, int] Gmsh node tag -> solver node ID. solver_to_gmsh_node : dict[int, int] Solver node ID -> Gmsh node tag. gmsh_to_solver_elem : dict[int, int] Gmsh element tag -> solver element ID. solver_to_gmsh_elem : dict[int, int] Solver element ID -> Gmsh element tag.

    def summary(self) -> str:

    return (
        f"NumberedMesh({self.method}): "
        f"{self.n_nodes} nodes, {self.n_elems} elements, "
        f"bandwidth={self.bandwidth}"
